extraction.name: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for chart question answering with 9,608 human-written questions and 23,111 machine-generated questions over 20,882 charts from Statista, Pew, OWID, and OECD, focusing on visual and logical reasoning.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Statista, OWID, and OECD, the underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted; for Pew, only chart images were crawled because underlying data tables were not available. Human-authored QA pairs were collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk, and additional QA pairs were generated from human-written chart summaries using a T5 model and then manually validated for quality assurance.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled since the underlying data tables were not available.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available chart images and chart-related materials from Statista, Pew Research, OWID, and OECD, including underlying data tables where available, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For machine-generated QA, a pre-trained T5 model was fine-tuned on SQuAD to generate answers and questions from human-written chart summaries. Invalid generated questions were filtered using a heuristic that removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table. Test sets of the machine-generated dataset were manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Charts were curated from four sources, and for the non-Pew sources the underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions were extracted. Bounding boxes of chart elements were extracted from SVG files. For annotation, workers were selected with at least 95% acceptance rate and 5,000 completed HITs, and further filtered with a pre-test. Human-written QA pairs were validated by a second annotator; exact matches were used to accept answers, otherwise answers were manually checked.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to create two QA pairs per chart image focusing on compositional questions (at least two mathematical/logical operations) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, and length). Each chart also had two previously asked questions verified by another worker. For each chart, the workers provided two questions with answers, and a second annotator answered the same questions. If both answers matched exactly, the answer was accepted; otherwise, the final answer was manually checked. Machine-generated QA pairs were created from human-written chart summaries using T5 and then manually validated on a subset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Exact-match agreement between crowd workers was 61.04%. A manual check on 500 random samples found agreement of 78.55% when typos and lexical variations were considered. For machine-generated QA, 1,250 QA pairs were manually analyzed and 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct after filtering.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were selected with an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 completed HITs; no other demographics were reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model for generating questions and answers from chart summaries; ChartOCR for extracting chart data tables; CRAFT for text recognition; Mask R-CNN for visual feature extraction; detectron2 was used to implement object detection.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No sensitive human attributes were collected as dataset fields; the paper notes only that annotator annotations were anonymized. The dataset includes chart topics such as politics, economy, health, society, and demographic trends.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note that the models could be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is diverse across four sources, but politics is a common topic, especially in Pew where nearly half of charts are about U.S. Politics & Policy. The benchmark also contains more unique tokens and informal language/typos, and visual references commonly focus on color and length.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Performance is lower than on previous datasets, indicating the challenge of human-written visual and logical reasoning questions. Automatic data extraction from real-world charts remains error-prone, especially for charts with diverse styles, pie charts, logarithmic-scale charts, and charts with large values. Nested arithmetic operations are not effectively handled by the models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation for chart question answering, including training, validation, and testing of models for visual and logical reasoning over charts; also used for pretraining/fine-tuning transfer experiments.
